thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High GPU queue growth and autoscaler failures in private-vpc cluster eu-west-2-prod-south. Impact: model inference latency > 10s for customers on private deployments. Trigger: sustained GPU pool saturation. Please acknowledge.

devendra_oncall: Ack. I'm looking. Root cluster eu-west-2-prod-south — seeing kernel-level queue spike and pods pending for >5m.

maria_ops: Confirming, dashboards show GPU utilization at 99-100% across all pools. Inflight request queue up ~1200. Autoscaler logs show repeated provisioning attempts but backoffs.

kevin_support: Any customer-facing impact? Which customers on that cluster?

julia_pm: Two enterprise customers on Dedicated->Private bridging are experiencing 500s and timeouts. Support ticket ids: #C-22341, #C-22342. They started reporting errors ~18m ago.

devendra_oncall: Quick technical summary: autoscaler creating nodes but kubelet-imagedownloads timeouts, then provider returns "quota_exceeded" for certain instance types. Also provisioning stuck because node bootstrap script fails on AMI validation (customers using locked AMI profile). Logs snippets: ```text
autoscaler: attempt 12 -> create instance i-0a... -> error: quota_exceeded
bootstrap: AMI mismatch: expected 2025-09-01-ami-xyz but customer-locked 2024-11-03-ami-abc -> abort
```

maria_ops: There's also a concurrent rate limit step in cloud provider for that account—looks like provider started throttling new instance API calls. That explains partial create + eventually backoff.

devendra_oncall: Immediate mitigation steps I'm doing: 1) Disable autoscaler for GPU pool to stop noisy retries, 2) Manually spin up fallback CPU-only nodepool for low-priority workloads, 3) Route degraded customer traffic to hosted fallback model variant. Executing now.

devendra_oncall: Command run: ```sh
# disable autoscaler on pool gpu-prod-south
redctl cluster update --cluster eu-west-2-prod-south --pool gpu-prod-south --autoscale=off
# create fallback cpu pool
redctl pool create --cluster eu-west-2-prod-south --name cpu-fallback --instance-type c6i.large --replicas 6
```

maria_ops: I have enabled routing fallback in the control plane for the affected customer routes: ```yaml
routes:
  - match: ".*/inference"
    fallback_model: "redwood-hosted/gpt-7b-cpu"
    activation: immediate
```

kevin_support: Thx. I'm updating the two affected customer tickets — I'm telling them we've activated a temporary CPU fallback and are working on restoring GPU capacity; ETA 45-90m for full recovery. Will ask if they want to pause heavy batch jobs.

julia_pm: Please add a short customer note: "We're seeing GPU provisioning delays in your private cluster due to AMI/quotas. We've enabled a temporary fallback and are prioritizing replacement capacity." Keep me posted for executive summary.

devendra_oncall: Observed side-effect: falling back to CPU model increases per-request latency and cost. I marked this as a temporary quality degradation only for non-SLA routes. Core low-latency routes kept on best-effort.

sre_bot: Event: autoscaler cpu/gpu create throttled -> rate_limit_exceeded. EventID: evt-83421. Attached logs to thread.

maria_ops: Investigations show cluster pool config has a constraint tag `customer_ami_lock:true` that prevents using the latest verified AMI — that forced the bootstrap into an older image that fails newer kubelet versions. Also cloud account quotas: GPU instance family limit at 8, attempts to create more hit account limit.

devendra_oncall: Next actions: 1) Request temporary quota bump from cloud provider (submitted ticket #CLD-7782). 2) Coordinate with infra to patch AMI constraints for affected customer (holding change until approval). 3) If provider won't grant immediate quota, we'll repoint heavier workloads to other regions where capacity exists.

maria_ops: I've started an emergency cross-region capacity check: `redctl capacity check --model gpu --region all | sort -k2 -n` — looks like us-east-1 and eu-central-1 have spare GPU capacity.

kevin_support: Customer asked if we can migrate them — they want to avoid config changes. I'll ask for permission to perform an automatic region fallback for their non-sensitive workloads.

julia_pm: Noted. Only proceed if customer's data residency allows it. Please get consent before changing region.

devendra_oncall: Manual quick-fixes applied: disabled noisy autoscaler retries, created CPU fallback pool, enabled routing fallback, requested quota bump. Monitoring queue length. Current queue down from 1200 -> 480 within 8 minutes after routing fallback.

maria_ops: Dashboard snapshot: 10m window: GPU queue: 1200 -> 480. Latency p95 for affected routes: 14s -> 9s (post-fallback).

kevin_support: Posting update to customers: "Temporary fallback activated; we are provisioning additional GPU capacity. Some requests may be slower; we're prioritizing your production endpoints." :pray:

sre_bot: Alert suppressed for gpu-pool-saturation in eu-west-2-prod-south (auto-snooze 30m) as mitigations in place.

devendra_oncall: I'm assigning follow-ups: - maria_ops to finish AMI constraint remediation (ticket INF-4921) - infra to chase quota CLD-7782 - kevin_support to confirm customer region fallback consent - julia_pm to prepare exec blurb. Handoff to next oncall in 20m.

maria_ops: Quick note on root cause hypothesis: customer_ami_lock + cloud provider quota + image download slowness (bad mirror) formed a three-way failure mode. We'll add a safety check in autoscaler: if repeated create failures with AMI mismatch, escalate before repeated retries.

devendra_oncall: Oncall handoff -> @maria_ops in 20. Leaving the CPU fallback active until GPU capacity restored or until we validate AMI patch. If we have to, we'll perform controlled region failover for non-sensitive traffic.

kevin_support: Customer reply: "OK to use hosted fallback and to move non-PII workloads to eu-central-1 if needed." They asked for hourly updates.

julia_pm: Thanks team. Please leave timeline + actions in the incident doc. I'll assemble a short postmortem template after we stabilize.

devendra_oncall: Final note before handoff: watch for autoscaler re-enable — do not re-enable GPU autoscaler until AMI lock and quota resolved, otherwise we'll re-trigger the loop. Marking manual flag: `autoscaler:disable:reason=ami-quota-loop`.

incident-bot: Handoff reminder: next oncall is maria_ops. Please acknowledge within 15m.

maria_ops: Ack. Taking over. Will escalate if GPU capacity not restored within 60m. :thumbsup:
